company.description: Client company name. Invent a relevant sample name only when missing and flag it in review notes.

provider.description: Provider business name; default CLIKWORKS unless operator specifies another.

fee.description: Total pilot fee with currency symbol. Default $5,000 only if no current scoped fee is provided; distinguish historical numbers.

duration.description: Total pilot duration. Default 45 days only when missing.

leads.description: Total leads in pilot scope. Default 3,000 only when missing. Do not confuse emails with leads or an initial cohort with total scope.

status.description: Short proposal status. Never say agreed unless explicitly accepted. Use SAMPLE OFFER if scope was declined or invented.

summary.default: Build a relevant prospect list, test a clear offer, and find out whether cold email can start useful sales conversations.
summary.description: One plain-language sentence: client sells WHAT to WHOM, and what this email pilot will test. Do not claim results.

problem.default: You need a repeatable way to reach the right buyers, without adding more manual prospecting to the team’s day.

hypothesis.default: Test a focused audience and a small set of messages. Use the replies to learn which buyer problems and offers resonate.
hypothesis.description: Tentative test hypothesis about the CLIENT offer, not the products sold by their target customers. Use aim or test, never will increase or benchmarks.

audience.default: Agree the geography, company size, buyer roles, and exclusions together before building the first list.
audience.description: The buyers of the CLIENT product. Distinguish target companies from their vendors. For gifting, roles buy gifts or swag, not martech. Include only supported geography, employee size and role details.

scope_note.default: Sample scope for testing. Final audience, budget, and timeline need review before kickoff.

scope_intro.default: We handle research and campaign execution. Your team supplies the offer, approvals, and timely sales follow-up.

work1.default: Confirm the ideal customer, buyer roles, exclusions, and a small sample before scaling research.

work2.default: Research suitable prospects, check current roles and email validity, and remove duplicates and exclusions.

work3.default: Write focused messages and follow-ups. Check existing domains and inboxes before deciding what else is needed.

work4.default: Launch after approval, review human replies, and refine the audience and message as evidence comes in.

client1.default: Share customer examples, approved claims, account access, and do-not-contact lists.
client1.description: A concrete action the CLIENT must take: share access, examples, approved offer and exclusions. This is a responsibility, not a descriptive fact.

client2.default: Review the target sample and copy. Name one person who can approve changes.
client2.description: A concrete CLIENT responsibility for sample-list and copy approvals with a named owner or owner to confirm.

client3.default: Own buyer follow-up, discovery calls, quotations, and fulfilment.
client3.description: A concrete CLIENT responsibility for buyer follow-up, calls, quotes and fulfilment.

launch_gate.default: We agree the audience, offer, copy, sending readiness, and reply owner before launch. No campaign starts without approval.

exclusions.default: Website work, full CRM rebuilds, paid ads, and sales closing are outside this pilot unless separately agreed.

timeline_intro.default: The pilot runs for 45 days from kickoff, with launch dependent on list quality, approvals, and sending readiness.

phase1_days.description: Contiguous numbered DAY RANGE covering this phase, e.g. Days 01–10. Three phases must cover the total duration.

phase1.default: Review the setup, agree the audience, check a sample list, and approve the first messages.

phase2_days.description: Contiguous numbered DAY RANGE covering this phase, e.g. Days 01–10. Three phases must cover the total duration.

phase2.default: Launch at a safe pace, review human replies, and check whether the right buyers are responding.

phase3_days.description: Contiguous numbered DAY RANGE covering this phase, e.g. Days 01–10. Three phases must cover the total duration.

phase3.default: Refine the offer and targeting, document the results, and agree what should happen next.

timing_note.default: If access, approvals, or inbox readiness cause delays, agree a revised schedule before sending.

metric1.default: Company fit, role fit, current employment, exclusions, and email verification are separate checks.
metric1.description: Clear numerator and denominator for human reply rate: unique human respondents / unique people reached, exclude automatic responses.

metric2.default: Unique human respondents divided by unique people reached. Exclude automatic replies.
metric2.description: Clear numerator and denominator for positive reply share: interested human respondents / human respondents.

metric3.default: Interested respondents divided by human respondents, with counts and examples alongside the percentage.

metric4.default: Track qualified conversations and next steps. Revenue can follow after the pilot ends.

success.default: Use list quality, relevant replies, and sales conversations to judge the test. No reply rate, meeting count, or revenue outcome is guaranteed.
success.description: Non-guaranteed test targets only if discussed; distinguish targets from promised outcomes.

commercial_intro.default: This is a proposal for review. Confirm the scope and assumptions together before committing.
commercial_intro.description: State if the client rejected the managed fee and prefers an audit. Say this is a sample managed option, NOT a smaller or accepted commitment.

payment.description: Payment terms. Default full advance before kickoff; flag as operator default when not in call.

included.default: Research, email checks, copy, campaign setup, management, and reporting for the agreed scope.

tools.default: Tool costs are to be confirmed before kickoff. Existing client-owned sending accounts stay with the client.
tools.description: Tool-cost inclusion and ownership from call. If unclear say to confirm, never invent vendor pricing.

ownership.default: The checked lead list, approved copy, campaign results, and access to your own sending accounts.

outside.default: Sales closing and fulfilment remain with your team. Additional work or tools need approval before purchase.

commercial_note.default: Missing commercial details are sample assumptions, not evidence of client approval. Confirm billing, tool costs, and any cancellation terms before kickoff.
commercial_note.description: Prominently preserve the exact budget objection and preferred immediate next step; do not soften cannot afford into sensitivity. Otherwise clear assumptions and open commercial terms.

next1.default: Review the proposal and resolve any open scope or budget questions.

next2.default: Confirm the agreement and payment, then share access and exclusions.

next3.default: Approve the sample audience and messages before launch.
next3.description: Final client-facing next step. Do not name an internal team member, subcontractor or proposed referral.

final_note.default: A pilot is a test, not a performance guarantee. Nothing renews automatically.
final_note.description: Short client-facing approval/assumption note. Do not name internal collaborators.
